## Academic leadership {#academic-leadership}

::: {.timeline}
::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
[Chairperson (Founding Secretary)]{.role}
[Sep 2023 – Jun 2026]{.when}
:::
[USIU-Africa EpiBio Club]{.org}

- Co-founded the club as Secretary, then served as Chairperson.
- Led a GIS workshop on using environmental exposure indices, WASH data and spatial modelling to map and predict cholera outbreaks in Kenya's informal settlements.
- Organised campus awareness drives during the Mpox (July 2025) and Ebola (June 2026) outbreak periods.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
[Electoral College Representative]{.role}
[Sep 2024 – Sep 2025]{.when}
:::
[School of Pharmacy & Health Sciences, USIU-Africa · team of three]{.org}

- Drafted and pushed through a mandatory **Hepatitis B vaccination** policy for health sciences students, then ran a drive that vaccinated an initial **84 high-risk students**.
- Organised a four-day blood drive with the Children Sickle Cell Foundation and the Red Cross Club, collecting **200+ pints** for children with sickle cell disease.
- Proposed a central academic data repository for epidemiology students, and secured fee interest waivers for affected student cohorts.

## Community health {#community-health}

::: {.timeline}
::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
[Project Lead]{.role}
[Apr 2023 – Jan 2024]{.when}
:::
[Action for Change · Kibera Initiative, Nairobi · with Angaza Foundation]{.org}

- Led a two-part socio-economic intervention responding to economic vulnerability and transactional relationships in Kibera, starting from **$350** in seed funding.
- Trained and equipped **28 young mothers** in bookkeeping and mobile hair braiding. Their braiding group generated **$500** in compounding profit within three months, and we then handed full control to the women.
- Fully equipped a youth football team as an alternative to crime. The team **won the Kibera league** three months later.

[Read the full project story →](leadership/kibera-initiative.qmd){.entry-link}
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-head}
[Founder & Lead, Community Health Project]{.role}
[Dec 2024 – Dec 2025]{.when}
:::
[Diagnostic Initiative · Batoukop, West Cameroon]{.org}

- Secured about $1,000 in funding to equip a local clinic, so residents of this low-resource community no longer had to travel for basic diagnostic tests.
- Designed and ran a one-month free testing clinic, producing the community's first systematic disease prevalence data (58% malaria positivity, 71% Widal positivity).
- Analysed the diagnostic data, found high rates of anemia (5% severe, 28% mild), and recommended clinical follow-up and referral pathways.

[Read the full project story →](projects/batoukop-diagnostics.qmd){.entry-link}
:::
:::
